critical_code_review_comments: brain_routes.py::_owned_account correctly enforces {user_id: caller} for non-admins and bypasses for admin — matches the pattern used by portfolio_ep/regime_ep.
transaction_costs._realized_deal_cost_r accepts user_id kwarg and both call sites in expected_cost_r pass it — defence-in-depth is complete.
decision_context.record_stage uses count_documents({...}, limit=MAX_STAGES) — efficient bounded check, not a race-free hard cap but adequate for defence-in-depth against internal writer misuse.

Minor: costs_ep passes account_id string to expected_cost_r after _owned_account verified it — good; note that the endpoint has no live signal so risk_per_lot is None → realized_deals branch never resolves via this route (only via account_config which also needs risk_per_lot). This means the endpoint always falls back to default commission when there's no live signal. Not a bug for iter-210, but worth remembering.

context_for_next_testing_agent: iter-210 changes had ripple effect on two iter-209 tests — I fixed them (test-only, not code). If future agents run these on a machine where broker_deals for a test account_id lack user_id, the realized_deals branch will silently return default — that's the intended defence-in-depth behaviour. The costs endpoint alone can never resolve realized_deals without a live signal (no risk_per_lot) — this is a known property, not a bug. Full backend suite (~560 tests) was not fully re-run due to 120s bash timeout — but the targeted 554 all pass, and one flaky order-dependent failure (test_iter111_corrections::test_worst_active_account_drives_stability) is unrelated to iter-210 and passes in isolation.
rca of the issue: Original BOLA: costs_ep did not enforce account ownership → any authenticated user could pass another user's 24-hex account_id and receive median commission/swap per lot + trade-activity samples for that account. Fix confirmed: brain_routes.costs_ep now calls _owned_account(db, user, account_id) which restricts non-admins to {_id: <oid>, user_id: caller.id} in db.accounts and raises 404 otherwise. Defence-in-depth: transaction_costs._realized_deal_cost_r now also scopes db.broker_deals queries by user_id, so even if the route check were bypassed the aggregation would return no data. Reproduction: as user A GET /api/brain/costs?symbol=XAUUSD&account_id=<B's oid> → 404 (verified). Owner (B) → 200. Admin → 200 (intentional bypass, consistent with portfolio/regime endpoints).
